title: Root nonce is a strictly increasing odometer
statement: SmartAccount.root_nonce increases by exactly 1 on every successful root instruction and never decreases, so no assertion is consumable twice.
spec_ref: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-warden-wallet-design.md#4 (root nonce = an odometer, not a set)
notes: Monotonicity is item (3) on the L6 Certora proof order; until then this is test-covered only. Storage is O(1): there is no consumed-nonce set to grow.

title: Strict n+1 equality, not a window
statement: A transcript whose root_nonce is not exactly equal to the stored value is rejected; there is no acceptance window and no replay bitmap.
notes: Do not replace with a set- or window-based scheme; strict n+1 is what makes a captured assertion dead the instant any other root instruction lands.

title: Slot-based root freshness
statement: A root ceremony is accepted only while signed_slot <= Clock::slot < signed_slot + MAX_ROOT_SLOT_AGE (150): a future slot is rejected outright and an age of exactly 150 slots is rejected.
notes: Landed by Task 0 (F) in 26a8c1e. Both halves of the inequality are covered by named boundary tests: age 0 and 149 accepted, 150 rejected, future-by-one rejected, u64::MAX treated as future rather than overflowing. `valid_expiry_does_not_rescue_a_stale_slot` and its mirror prove the two clocks are independent bounds, not alternatives.

title: Wall-clock expiry is the secondary bound
statement: expiry_ts must satisfy now <= expiry_ts <= now + 600s; an expired transcript and one expiring beyond the 600s horizon are both rejected, and the 600s boundary itself is accepted.
notes: Clock::unix_timestamp is a stake-weighted estimate; once WRD-NONCE-03 lands this stays only as the secondary bound and as the sole bound on 1C's deferred queue/execute_pending path.

title: Cap dominance
statement: Every accepted spend satisfies amount <= min(per_tx, per_day - spent_today, per_30d - sum(ring)), and for a session additionally lifetime_spent + amount <= lifetime_cap.
notes: Item (2) on the L6 Certora proof order. Not yet mutation-tested: cargo-mutants is unpiloted on this workspace (spec 17 L4), and buckets.rs is the designated pilot module.

title: Bucket accounting is exact and the ring self-cleans
statement: spent_today equals the sum of the day's debits, sum(ring) <= per_30d, and no ring slot survives a rollover that should have zeroed it.
notes: Item (1) on the L6 Certora proof order. Codex's own reimplementation of this ring in the 1A pilot wrote the closed day to ring[kept-1] instead of ring[RING_DAYS-1], permanently understating 30-day spend; the differential test is what caught it, so keep the reference model.

title: No cap means zero, never unlimited
statement: A mint with no cap entry (and a zeroed cap entry) permits outflow of exactly 0; the missing-cap branch rejects rather than skipping the check.
notes: find_cap must never match the all-zero default Pubkey, or an unconfigured slot silently becomes a cap for mint 11111...; that is asserted separately.

title: An expired or revoked session is exhausted, not absent
statement: A session past expiry_ts, with a stale generation_at_grant, revoked, or belonging to another account is treated as having zero remaining allowance on every axis, never as an account with no cap configured.
notes: This is the exact shape of LazorKit ACC-C2 (an authorisation branch that skipped a check instead of failing it) and it is the difference between a fail-closed and a fail-open wallet. Every new 1B comparison must be written the same way.

title: Root direct `transfer` is bounded like a session
statement: The root `transfer` path enforces outflow[mint] <= large_threshold[mint] per transaction AND debits the same account-wide day and rolling-30-day buckets that sessions debit.
notes: SCOPED TO `transfer` DELIBERATELY. The spec states the same rule for the root `execute` and `swap` paths, but no such path exists yet and no test covers it -- that is WRD-CAP-09, seeded separately at `unimplemented`. Rolling the two into one row would have let a 1A test stand as evidence for a 1B surface.

title: Debit is atomic
statement: A debit that is going to be rejected leaves every bucket field byte-identical to its pre-call value, including when the rejection happens after a day-boundary rollover or an arithmetic overflow guard fires.
notes: The rollover is the dangerous half: it mutates state before the cap comparison, so a non-atomic implementation would leak a free day of allowance on every rejected spend.

title: Day and 30-day windows are account-wide, not per session
statement: Every session and the root debit the same SmartAccount.buckets, so N sessions do not get N day caps; and a grant that sets a non-zero per-session per_day/per_30d is rejected rather than stored.
notes: 1B keeps rejecting per-session day caps at grant. Per-session day buckets are 1C and ride on the single DayBuckets PDA (spec 5.2 rule 4c).

title: Session lifetime cap is exact and survives a regrant
statement: lifetime_spent + amount <= lifetime_cap on every session spend, a regrant merges by mint while preserving spent, and a regrant that would set a lifetime cap below what has already been spent is rejected.
notes: prior_authority_hash is what makes the merge bind the authority it produces rather than only the fields it names; that is the LZR-ACC-H1 shape (accounts/fields omitted from the signed payload).

title: Root `execute` and `swap` are bounded like a session
statement: The root `execute` and `swap` paths enforce outflow[mint] <= large_threshold[mint] per transaction AND debit the same account-wide day and rolling-30-day buckets; anything larger must come from execute_pending, whose execution also debits the buckets.
notes: Split out of WRD-CAP-05 so a 1A `transfer` test can never stand as evidence for a 1B surface. The one-line consequence this row protects: a root attacker without guardians extracts at most the account-wide day bucket per day and the 30-day cap per month, across EVERY root path -- which is false the moment one root path skips the buckets.

title: ops_mask is bounded by the ceiling AND by the assigned bits
statement: A grant is rejected unless ops_mask is a subset of policy.session_ops_ceiling AND a subset of the bits this program version has actually assigned; an unassigned bit is refused rather than stored, and an operation whose bit is unset is rejected at use.
notes: The unassigned-bit refusal is the load-bearing half and is easy to omit: an unassigned bit stored today silently becomes real authority the day a later version assigns it. Refusing at grant, not at use, is what makes that impossible.

title: Session caps may not exceed the policy ceiling
statement: Every per-mint cap in a grant is <= policy.session_ceiling for that mint, a mint with no session ceiling cannot be granted at all, and the ceiling itself cannot be set above the account cap at creation.
notes: The boundary-accepted test matters as much as the rejections: an off-by-one that rejected a grant exactly AT the ceiling would be a silent usability bug nobody reports, and it is the same code path that an off-by-one in the other direction breaks security.

title: Session expiry is bounded and must be in the future
statement: A grant's expiry_ts must be strictly in the future and no later than now + policy.max_session_life; the max_session_life boundary itself is accepted, and a policy setting max_session_life above 30 days is refused at creation.
notes: Expiry is one of the three axes on which an expired session must read as EXHAUSTED rather than ABSENT (WRD-CAP-04); this row covers the grant-time bound, WRD-CAP-04 covers the use-time behaviour.

title: generation_at_grant is refreshed at grant and matched at use
statement: A grant records the account's current generation, a regrant refreshes it, and a session whose generation_at_grant does not equal the account's current generation cannot act.
notes: Same evidence caveat as WRD-ROOT-08: generation is advanced by a helper, not by a real execute_recovery (WRD-ROOT-11). This proves the match, not the bump.

title: A regrant binds the authority it produces, not only the fields it names
statement: A merging grant carries prior_authority_hash -- the hash of the retained identity, every cap slot and every lifetime cap it is allowed to merge into -- a mismatch is refused, a fresh grant must carry the zero sentinel, and a regrant must not carry it.
notes: This is the LZR-ACC-H1 lesson generalised: it is not enough for the signed payload to name the fields it changes; it must bind the state it merges into, or a signature over a partial view authorises an authority the signer never saw.

title: Only the root or the session itself may revoke it
statement: revoke_session succeeds for a root ceremony over that exact session and for the session key signing for itself, and fails for a stranger, for a root ceremony naming a different session account, and for a substituted rent-refund destination.
notes: The substituted-refund case is the rent-theft shape of LZR-ACC-H1 and the reason the deny-list treats CloseAccount as a value-moving instruction (WRD-DENY-01), not a housekeeping one.

title: program_allowlist_id must be 0 until the registry exists
statement: A grant carrying a non-zero program_allowlist_id is rejected in Phase 1A/1B, so no session can hold a dangling reference to a registry that does not exist yet.
notes: Reopens as WRD-REG-* when Task 3 lands the adapter registry: at that point the check inverts from `must be 0` to `must resolve`, and the negative test must invert with it rather than being deleted.

title: Grant shape limits are enforced, not assumed
statement: A grant carries at most MAX_CAPS_PER_GRANT = 2 caps, no duplicate mint, matching cap and lifetime-cap lengths, and an Ed25519 session key kind; a 2-cap grant transaction fits the 1232-byte packet.
notes: MAX_CAPS_PER_GRANT = 2 is a MEASURED byte bound (a 2-cap grant is 976 B of 1,232, and clientDataJSON may legally grow to 512 B), not a design preference. signed_slot (26a8c1e) consumed part of that headroom, so 1B must re-measure rather than assume the constant still holds.

title: Field-identity conservation on vault-owned token accounts
statement: For every account whose BEFORE snapshot is a vault-owned token account, every field except amount is byte-identical AFTER (runtime owner, token owner, mint, delegate, delegated_amount, close_authority, state, is_native, data_len, TLV-tail hash) and the after-state independently satisfies policy (state == Initialized, delegate == None, close_authority == None).
notes: Before/after, not after-only: a pre-existing delegate that the CPI CLEARS would pass an after-only check. COption tags decode strictly (0=None, 1=Some, anything else = parse error), never `tag != 0`. The 1A spike proved the comparison function by unit test only, never end to end through a real mutating CPI.

title: Outflow is coalesced per mint before a single debit
statement: outflow[mint] is summed across ALL vault-owned token accounts of that mint (negative = inflow, floored at 0 for cap purposes) and passed to exactly one buckets::debit call per mint per instruction.
notes: Per-account debiting would let N accounts of one mint each spend per_tx. The negative test is two vault ATAs of the same mint each draining just under per_tx.

title: The SOL equation counts each lamport exactly once
statement: outflow[SOL] = (pda_lamports_before - pda_lamports_after) + sum over vault NATIVE accounts of (account_lamports_before - account_lamports_after); a native account's value is its LAMPORTS, not its cached `amount` (which only moves on SyncNative); native lamports are counted here and are exempt from the lamports-unchanged rule; non-native CloseAccount rent enters only via the decoder's decoded close intents (spec 5.2 rule 4a).
notes: A permitted vault-sweep close returns rent as an increase in the PDA's own lamports, which the equation already sees; adding it again double-counts. The not-to-the-vault backstop (add lamports_before to outflow[SOL]) must be tested with the decoder stubbed out. WRDF-0011 (A0 round 7): native value is LAMPORTS, not the SyncNative-updated `amount` cache — the earlier amount_before-amount_after wording was the vulnerability. is_native must agree with the native mint key. Task 5 must wire the lamport-based equation and add a real-CPI SyncNative+Transfer regression.

title: Mint authority fields are byte-identical
statement: Whenever a vault-owned token account of mint M is writable, M's mint account must be present; if the vault holds any authority on M, every authority field (mint_authority, freeze_authority, and for Token-2022 transfer_fee_config_authority / withdraw_withheld_authority, extracted by TLV type and offset) is compared byte-for-byte and any change is an instruction reject, not an accounting entry.
notes: A whole-tail hash is NOT the mint control: legitimate transfer_fee accrual mutates withheld_amount in the same tail and would fail on the happy path. supply is snapshotted but is not an authority field.

title: A vault-owned token account may not disappear
statement: A vault-owned token account present BEFORE that does not exist or does not parse AFTER is a reject, unless the payload decoder handed the comparison a matching decoded close intent for that exact account; nothing downstream may infer a close from a disappearance.
notes: This is the control that catches a CloseAccount nested inside another program's CPI: the decoder cannot establish amount_before == 0 or the destination for a nested close, so it never emits an intent and the disappearance rejects here.

title: accounts_hash binds the logical list
statement: accounts_hash is computed over the LOGICAL account list in logical order (logical[0]=smart_account, logical[1]=signer, logical[2+k]=remaining_accounts[k]), hashing pubkey || is_signer || is_writable for each; no payload index ever refers to a physical slot and no code indexes the raw account slice.
notes: LZR-ACC-C1 is the nearest-miss: LazorKit bound accounts by index, not pubkey, so reordering the account list under a captured signature swapped the transfer recipient. Required negative tests: reorder accounts under a captured signature; duplicate a key in the logical list (a duplicate shifts every later index); omit an account the payload referenced.

title: No inner instruction may set a delegate on a vault-owned token account
statement: No inner instruction of execute may set, change or clear a delegate on a vault-owned token account, on either the session path or the root path.
notes: Doubly enforced by design: the deny-list rejects Approve/ApproveChecked/Revoke in the decoder (WRD-DENY-01) and the field-identity comparison rejects any delegate change reached another way (WRD-EXEC-01). Both controls must be tested independently so neither passes only because the other fired first.

title: Program owner is compared, not just field values
statement: The before/after snapshot compares each account's runtime program owner, so an account that is transferred out, closed and reopened under a program that fakes the SPL token byte layout fails the comparison.
notes: Swig's sign_v1 checked end-state field values (balance, mint, token-account owner FIELD) but never the account's actual program owner: transfer out -> close -> reopen under a fake-layout program passed every check, full drain from a 1-lamport-permission role. Snap.owner_program covers it -- the point of this entry is that it must be TESTED, not merely present.

title: Token-2022 danger extensions reject unconditionally in 1B
statement: permanent_delegate (12), transfer_hook (14) and confidential-transfer mints (4/5) reject unconditionally; transfer_fee (1) also rejects in 1B because the allow-list machinery is 1C. The decision is made by inspecting the mint's TLV, which is why the mint account must be present.
notes: Three classes, not two: (i) deny-never-allow-listable, (ii) allow-listable in 1C with an inequality, (iii) confidential transfer = permanent non-goal, unverifiable by construction, never a policy toggle. 1B's blanket reject is a TIGHTENING of this rule, not a different one.

title: Adapter-decoded max_in and a pinned source ATA bound the call
statement: Before any inner CPI runs, the adapter parses max_in out of the inner instruction's own data (never inferred from balances) and compares it against the session per_tx and the account buckets, and the adapter's role validator requires the inner instruction's source account to be the specific vault ATA the caller declared.
notes: DESIGN BET, not a proven property (spec 5.3). A net before/after snapshot at ANY granularity cannot observe a same-CPI round trip: 100 SOL out and 99.5 SOL back inside one CPI presents a net delta of 0.5. 1B introduces no gross_turnover field and no gross bucket. The product statement must not claim conservation bounds intra-CPI turnover.

title: `frozen` gates every 1A outflow and every grant
statement: While SmartAccount.frozen is set, no Phase 1A instruction that moves value or widens authority succeeds: `transfer` on both the session and the root path, and `grant_session`.
notes: SCOPED TO THE 1A SURFACES DELIBERATELY. `execute`, `swap` and `execute_pending` are covered by WRD-FRZ-03 at `unimplemented`; naming them here would have let 1A tests stand as evidence for instructions that do not exist. A frozen-gate negative test is on the acceptance checklist for each of them.

title: A freeze is not a brick
statement: rotate_nonce still succeeds while frozen, so the root can always prove liveness and reach unfreeze; freeze blocks value movement, not the root ceremony itself.
notes: The 1A unfreeze timelock is read LIVE from policy.timelock_secs at lift time. 1B's set_policy must make a deliberate choice for an already-frozen account: preserve the live read, or snapshot at freeze time. That decision opens a new invariant when it lands.

title: 1B value paths refuse while frozen
statement: execute, swap and execute_pending each refuse while frozen, re-validated against CURRENT state at execution rather than at queue time.
notes: execute_pending is permissionless after execute_after, so the frozen check is the only thing standing between a queued action and a freeze that landed after it was queued.

title: Proof of possession at account creation
statement: create_account cannot succeed without a valid root ceremony over the derived address, and the address itself is Keccak256("WARDEN/seed/v1" || root_pubkey33 || salt32) computed on-chain, so the PDA cannot be squatted with an attacker-controlled root: a different root derives a different address, and the victim's address cannot be reached without the victim's passkey.
notes: CLOSED by Phase 1B Task 2b. Also referred to as WRD-PoP-01 in the Phase 1B plan prose; WRD-ROOT-01 is the canonical id. RED evidence: at d0072fd an executable exploit created the victim's PDA under the attacker's root and locked the victim out (task-2b-report.md). The seed derivation is stronger than Squads' fix (require create_key to sign) because it needs no extra signer. Two Phase-1A gaps close with it: creation is now top-level-only, and an off-curve root x cannot be created because the precompile cannot verify a signature under a point it cannot decompress. Cost: MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE fell from 4 to 1 (see WRD-BUF-05). Keep the squat-race negative test forever. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: Root instructions are transaction-level only
statement: Every root instruction requires get_stack_height() == TRANSACTION_LEVEL_STACK_HEIGHT, so a root path can never be invoked through a middleman program.
notes: Landed in 26a8c1e. The negative test drives a real CPI caller (programs/test-middleman, test-only, never deployed) rather than stubbing the stack height, which is the only version of this test worth having. Distinct from the pre-existing self-CPI rejection, which only blocks warden->warden. Adopted from LazorKit (MIT). Held at test-covered, not higher: one caller shape is proven, not the whole space of intermediate programs.

title: User verification is mandatory
statement: authenticatorData must have both UP and UV set; a UP-only assertion is rejected.
notes: The credential is created with userVerification: required and ES256 only; the on-chain UV check is what makes that client-side request non-advisory.

title: rpIdHash is SHA-256 of the FULL origin, read from state
statement: rp_id_hash equals SHA-256("chrome-extension://<id>") -- not SHA-256("<id>") -- it is recomputed on-chain from the stored origin at creation, read from SmartAccount state on every verification, and never taken from caller-supplied instruction data or a compiled-in literal.
notes: The naive reading of the WebAuthn spec rejects EVERY assertion; measured in spike 2b. Open L9 lane, NOT covered by this invariant: the extension id changes between a dev-loaded and a store build and there is no migration path for an account created under the old one.

title: Precompile binding and ordering
statement: The root path binds exactly one secp256r1 precompile instruction, named by index in its own instruction data, at a lower index than the warden instruction, executed by the real secp256r1 program id, carrying exactly one signature whose (pubkey, message, signature) equal (root.pubkey, authenticatorData || SHA256(clientDataJSON), sig).
notes: L0 DEPENDENCY NOW SATISFIED (26a8c1e): programs/warden/tests/sigverify_wiring.rs asserts BOTH directions -- a valid signature makes the transaction succeed, and a forged one is rejected by the precompile, not by us. Only the pair proves the runtime actually runs ECDSA; either alone is compatible with a harness that verifies nothing. litesvm must stay pinned with the `precompiles` feature (LiteSVM::default() starts with every feature off) and .claude/test-gate.sh additionally asserts the feature RESOLVES -- which is a different failure mode from the runtime gate, so both are required. `fee_payer_identity_neither_authorizes_nor_blocks` is the control that stops the whole suite passing on the outer transaction signature.

title: Strict depth-0 clientDataJSON scanner
statement: clientDataJSON is rejected above MAX_CLIENT_DATA_LEN (512 B); the object is walked at depth 0 only; exactly one top-level type/challenge/origin is required and any duplicate top-level key rejects; JSON escapes are decoded before comparison or the value is rejected; type == "webauthn.get"; origin equals the stored origin; challenge equals base64url(transcript hash); a present crossOrigin must be the JSON boolean false. Byte-substring matching is forbidden.
notes: LazorKit's regression vector {"tokenBinding":{"id":"x}y"},"challenge":"real"} -- a } inside a nested string desynced their brace-depth tracker and mis-located challenge -- is ported and rejected. This is one of the two designated Trident fuzz targets (L4); the other is the 1B ExecutePayload parser.

title: cluster_tag domain separation
statement: cluster_tag is a 32-byte client-attested domain separator stored at creation, non-zero-checked, immutable in 1A, and bound into the transcript so an assertion produced against one stored tag cannot be replayed against an account holding a different tag.
notes: STATED LIMIT: it is NOT a verified genesis binding. A Solana program cannot read the cluster's genesis hash, so the value is whatever the extension wrote at create_account. It does not guarantee the tag names the cluster the transaction lands on. Codex flagged this in the 1A pilot as a finding; it was adjudicated a false positive because transcript.rs:69-76 documents the deferral -- in a file the reviewer had not been shown. That is why sibling files are now mandatory in every review prompt.

title: Generation-bump semantics (helper-driven)
statement: A transcript carrying a generation other than the account's current generation is rejected, and a session's authority is scoped to the generation it was granted under.
notes: EVIDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: the covering tests advance `generation` through a test helper / a revoke-and-regrant cycle, NOT through a real `execute_recovery`. They prove the CHECK, not the BUMP. The property that actually matters to a user -- that recovery invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- is WRD-ROOT-11, seeded at `unimplemented` because `execute_recovery` is Phase 1C and does not exist.

title: action_hash binds the complete semantic inputs
statement: action_hash = Keccak256(op_type:u8 || borsh(op_args)) where op_args contains every semantic input of the instruction the root authorises; the program recomputes it from the instruction it is executing and rejects on mismatch, so no argument or account can be swapped after the passkey ceremony.
notes: The op_type byte is the discriminator LZR-ACC-M2 was missing; op_bytes_are_distinct + op_bytes_are_pinned keep it from collapsing. 1B extends op_args to execute/swap (the exact compiled instruction list, or the Stage hash) and that re-opens this invariant for those ops.

title: Transcript preimage byte layout is pinned across the language boundary
statement: transcript_hash = Keccak256("WARDEN/root/v1" || cluster_tag[32] || program_id[32] || account[32] || generation:u64LE || policy_version:u32LE || root_nonce:u64LE || expiry_ts:i64LE || signed_slot:u64LE || action_hash[32]), and the Rust program, the packages/core TS mirror and the IDL agree on it byte for byte.

evidence.name: does not treat expiryTs and signedSlot as interchangeable

notes: HELD DOWN DELIBERATELY -- the layout is right, the GATE is missing. 26a8c1e added signed_slot to Rust, the packages/core mirror and the IDL together, and both sides pin vectors including a max-slot one and an adjacency test (expiry_ts and signed_slot are adjacent fixed-width integers, so a mirror that swapped them would still hash something). But the vectors are HAND-SYNCED: the TS test hard-codes hex copied from the Rust test, so a coordinated edit to both drifts silently and nothing fails. Only a generated cross-language golden-vector gate (Task 9 / L9) promotes this row. LZR-ACC-H2 is exactly this class.

title: Recovery invalidates everything outstanding
statement: A successful execute_recovery replaces the root and increments generation, and that increment invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- proven end to end through the real instruction, not a test helper.
notes: Seeded now because WRD-ROOT-08's evidence advances `generation` via a helper and a revoke/regrant cycle, which proves the CHECK but not the BUMP. Without this row the ledger would read as if recovery invalidation were already covered. Phase 1C.

title: Fixed deny-list, on both paths, above the registry
statement: SetAuthority, Approve, ApproveChecked and Revoke on SPL Token and Token-2022 are rejected in the execute payload decoder on BOTH the session and the root path, before dispatch and before any registry lookup; CloseAccount is rejected unless ALL of: it is a direct payload instruction (not nested inside another program's CPI), the account's amount_before is exactly 0, the decoded destination is the SmartAccount PDA, and the account is neither the PDA itself nor a Mint.
notes: Instruction tags (SetAuthority 6, Approve 4, Revoke 5, CloseAccount 9, ApproveChecked 13) are UNVERIFIED against SPL source. The implementer re-derives each from spl-token's TokenInstruction enum at the pinned crate version, records crate version + source path in docs/program/PHASE1B-MEASUREMENTS.md, and a unit test asserts each constant equals what the crate encodes. A wrong tag here is a silent hole, not a compile error. The decoder is a whitelist of closes it can PROVE, not a blacklist of closes it dislikes.

title: No registry entry can re-enable a denied pair
statement: A registry (or policy) list containing a denied (program, instruction) pair still fails closed: the decoder runs first, there is no override flag, and the deny-list is unreachable by the section 5.4 loosening lattice.
notes: Section 5.4 says loosening EXTENDS the registry, so a deny that lived only in the registry would not be a floor at all -- and the root path skips the registry entirely, so a deny enforced at registry_allows would not cover the root path in any form. The required negative test is a registry list containing SetAuthority that still fails closed.

title: A squatted Stage is recoverable
statement: A stranger who pre-opens a Stage PDA at our content hash cannot permanently block staging: the Stage carries an expiry_ts, anyone may close it after expiry, and the rent goes to the squatter who paid it.
notes: Task 4. Two firms with two methods hit this exact class on Squads: Neodyme ND-SQD3-LO-01 (TransactionBuffer seeded [multisig, buffer_index], 256 slots, one Initiate-permission member fills all 256 with unclosable garbage) and Certora H-01 (transaction buffer may become inaccessible and unclosable). Seeds must bind the creator, or the count must be unbounded-but-cleanable -- pick one and test the other's failure mode.

title: No unbounded uncleanable buffer
statement: There is no per-account fixed slot table an attacker can exhaust, and every Stage account has at least one permissionless path to closure that returns rent to whoever funded it.
notes: Task 4. The vault must never fund Stage rent (spec 5.2 rule 4: account creation is always funded by the outer fee payer), or the squat becomes a rent drain of the shape audited on revoke_session.

title: Every root-ceremony transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A complete root ceremony transaction (secp256r1 precompile instruction + the warden instruction) serialises to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232 for freeze, unfreeze, a 2-cap grant_session, and root transfer of SOL and of an SPL token.
notes: The budget is tight: the 1A root ceremony uses 680 B, leaving ~552 B of payload headroom, and clientDataJSON may legally grow to 512 B. WRD-NONCE-03's signed_slot consumes part of that headroom -- 1B RE-MEASURES and these tests must be re-run, not assumed.

title: Every session transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A session-signed transfer of SOL and of an SPL token each serialise to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232.
notes: The 40-account cap on session execute is PROVISIONAL and byte-driven, not CU-driven: a real 43-account Jupiter route serialised to 1,235 B while a 35-account route fit. That 35-43 band is a totalKeys measurement; writableKeys and executeAccountCount were never captured. 1B must re-derive it.

title: create_account packet limits are measured, not assumed
statement: A create_account transaction carrying its mandatory proof-of-possession ceremony fits the 1232-byte packet at MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE = 1 mint (cap + ceiling + threshold) and does NOT fit at 2, and more than MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE mints is rejected on-chain.
notes: Re-measured for Phase 1B Task 2b: proof of possession adds 477 B (182 B precompile instruction, 226 B RootArgs, the Instructions sysvar account), so 0 mints = 949 B, 1 mint = 1117 B, 2 mints = 1285 B (53 B over) and MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE dropped 4 -> 1. Mints 2..8 are added later by Phase 1C set_policy. The negative tests are the load-bearing half: they are what stops a future constant bump from producing unlandable transactions. create_with_pop_transaction_sizes_are_measured_and_bounded asserts the constant EQUALS the largest count that actually fits, so it cannot drift from the measurement. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: Staged content is bound to generation and policy_version and consumed on use
statement: stage_finalize records generation and policy_version and checks Keccak256(content) == hash; execution requires both to equal the current values and closes the Stage on use, so staged content is single-use and cannot survive a recovery or a policy change.
notes: Task 4. TOB-SQUADS-8 is the adjacent class: ephemeral signer seeds derived only from the batch key rather than per transaction, so all transactions in a batch shared one ephemeral keypair. Any PDA whose seeds do not uniquely bind (tx index, creator, nonce) reproduces it -- which is why Stage addressing and execute's invoke_signed seeds are both in scope here.

title: Unit layer: per-mint net outflow, coalesced and floored
statement: compare_and_account returns outflow per mint computed from before/after snapshots: multiple vault ATAs of one mint coalesce into a single entry, intra-vault rebalances net to zero, and inflow floors to zero rather than crediting a negative outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY (campaign plan G7): synthetic snapshots, no CPI in the loop. End-to-end enforcement through execute is WRD-EXEC-*, unimplemented until Task 5. Added retrospectively by A0; the module landed in Task 1 (f0f38ca, fixes 2023902/d394b74).

title: Unit layer: one SOL equation across WSOL and PDA lamports
statement: Wrapped-SOL value is measured by LAMPORTS, not the cached `amount`, and is decided by `is_native` (which must agree with the native mint key or the account is rejected); wrapped-SOL and PDA lamport deltas merge into one SOL number, floored once, and a native mint key never appears in by_mint.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. Non-WSOL CloseAccount rent folds into the same SOL sum (a_close_to_a_stranger_charges_the_rent_as_sol_outflow). See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. WRDF-0008 (A0 round 3): classification was mint-key-only and would have split a Token-2022 native account's delta into by_mint[9pan…]; fixed to is_native-first with both native mint keys as belt-and-braces (compare.rs account_amount, constants::NATIVE_MINT_2022 verified against vendored spl-token-2022 7.0.0 src/native_mint.rs). RED verified: the new test fails against the pre-fix classification. WRDF-0011 (A0 round 6): native value was measured by `amount`, a SyncNative-updated cache — a SyncNative+Transfer pair drained an unsynced donation with amount unchanged. Now measured by lamports, and is_native must agree with the native mint key (mismatch rejected). RED verified.

title: Unit layer: authority or identity mutation is a reject, never an accounting entry
statement: Any change to a vault token account's owner, delegate, close authority, state, is_native, data length, TLV tail, runtime program owner, or backing-mint identity/authorities is InstructionRejected/ConservationViolated — it is never converted into an outflow number; pre-existing delegates and close authorities reject even when unchanged.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. owner_program in Snap is what closes the SWIG-ACC-C1 fake-layout class at this layer; the through-CPI test is Task 5's swig_acc_c1_close_and_reopen_under_fake_layout_rejected. WRDF-0012 (A0 round 6): several unmodeled T22 mint extensions (MintCloseAuthority, InterestBearingConfig, MetadataPointer, group/member pointers, ScaledUiAmountConfig, PausableConfig) carry reassignable authorities no compared field would see, and the mint tail hash is never compared; 1B now fails closed on any required mint with an unmodeled extension. RED verified.

title: Unit layer: accounts cannot appear, vanish, or move without an explanation
statement: A vault token account that disappears without a matching CloseIntent, appears vault-owned only in the AFTER snapshot, changes list position, or duplicates another pubkey is rejected; a legal vault-sweep close is counted once and only once.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. The became-vault-owned rejection (NewVaultAccountRejected, 6051) is round-1 fix C2, evidenced here directly. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. Prior art corrected per WRDF-0005: LZR-ACC-C1 is the position-vs-identity class; TOB-SQUADS-7 (unauthenticated creation) belongs to WRD-ROOT-01, not here.

title: Unit layer: strict, fail-closed SPL / Token-2022 layout parsing
statement: Classic SPL parses only exactly 82-byte mints and 165-byte token accounts; COption tags other than 0/1 are parse errors; T22 TLV tails are walked bounded and fail closed, danger extensions each set their bit, and transfer-fee authorities are extracted by TLV type rather than hashed with the whole tail.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. spl_crate_layout_lengths_are_pinned ties the 82/165 constants to the pinned spl-token crate so a dependency bump cannot silently move the layout. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Unit layer: conservation arithmetic cannot wrap
statement: Outflow summation uses checked arithmetic and rejects on overflow instead of wrapping; a crafted pair of snapshots whose deltas sum past u64::MAX is an error, not a small outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. clippy::arithmetic_side_effects is denied crate-wide as the static half of this claim. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Root key non-exportable, never in extension memory
statement: Warden exposes no root-export API and root private-key material never enters extension memory; session and recovery secrets are typed and cannot be used as root authority. (A platform-synced passkey may itself be backup-eligible and movable by the OS/authenticator — that is the T7 threat, outside Warden's enforcement; Warden's boundary is that IT never exports or holds root material.)
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan 2026-08-20); implemented by client C2. Unimplemented until apps/extension exists. WRDF-0024: narrowed from 'non-exportable' — a backup-eligible synced passkey is movable by the platform (WebAuthn L3 / FIDO); Warden's enforceable boundary is no export API + no root material in extension memory. Whether synced passkeys may be roots is the open T7 owner decision.

title: No retained password; no equality-check auth
statement: No plaintext password is retained after derivation; no password equality check substitutes for fresh cryptographic authentication.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2/C5.

title: Absolute wall-clock unlock deadlines
statement: Idle and hard unlock deadlines are absolute wall-clock values, checked on every key use and after every service-worker wake; expiry clears all session unlock material.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. MV3 worker suspension is the threat.

title: Versioned AEAD keyring envelope with contextual AAD
statement: Encrypted keyring envelopes are versioned AEAD with random nonces and AAD binding account, full extension origin, key kind, schema version, canonical cluster identity (genesis hash), and Warden program id; malformed, unknown-version, replayed-context (incl. cross-cluster), and tampered envelopes reject.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. AAD must not bind a per-release build hash (would brick old envelopes on update). WRDF-0023: AAD must include genesis + program id because a SmartAccount PDA is not network-qualified (same program+root+salt → same address across clusters); without them an envelope transplants between clusters undetected.

title: Browser-owned message provenance
statement: Privileged background methods derive origin, extension id, tab, and frame from browser-owned sender metadata, never page-supplied data.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C1 (the MV3 trust boundary).

title: Privileged UI port requires proven extension identity
statement: An extension UI port is privileged only when sender.id == chrome.runtime.id AND browser-owned sender.url/origin is the exact chrome-extension://<id> origin at an allowed extension-page path; extension-id equality alone is insufficient because an extension-owned content script shares sender.id and can call runtime.connect.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C1. WRDF-0021: id-equality alone lets a content script impersonate privileged UI (Chrome runtime docs); the origin+path check is required.

title: Immutable single-use approval record
statement: Every approval is an immutable, expiring, single-use background record binding request id, origin, account, method, cluster, serialized message bytes and digest.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C3. V4/U7 depend on this record.

title: Approval renders exact bytes; signer rechecks digest
statement: The approval UI renders from those exact bytes and the signer rechecks the digest immediately before signing; caller labels, route params, or stale simulation objects never define the displayed intent.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C3/C4.

title: Atomic single-winner approval resolution
statement: Concurrent approve/reject/timeout/navigation events have one atomic winner and cannot sign twice or resolve the wrong request.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C3.

title: Local decode of signed bytes; no blind-sign in v1
statement: Supported instructions are decoded locally from serialized bytes; unknown or ambiguous instructions never receive a benign verdict and there is no blind-sign fallback in v1.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C4.

title: Simulation/reputation bound to digest and freshness
statement: Every simulation/reputation result is bound to exact message digest, signer/account, cluster identity, and freshness; mismatch or absence cannot display a green/safe state.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C4. See WRD-QTE-01 for the swap-price-source case.

title: Simulator output is advisory only
statement: Simulator output is advisory and can neither authorize an on-chain-denied action nor bypass local/on-chain policy.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C4.

title: Fresh ceremony for any secret export
statement: Any recovery-secret reveal or export requires a fresh ceremony; Warden exposes no export path for root or session secrets and root material never enters extension memory; portable recovery envelopes retain the specified 128-bit secret strength and bind AAD to account, genesis hash, Warden program id, recovery-key context, and version (a SmartAccount PDA is not network-qualified, so account-only AAD transplants across clusters). (Platform passkey sync is outside this boundary — see WRD-KEY-01 and threat T7.)
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C5. WRDF-0024: 'never exportable' narrowed to Warden's enforceable boundary (no Warden export path); platform sync of a backup-eligible passkey is the T7 threat, not a Warden API. WRDF-0026: recovery-envelope AAD must include genesis + program id like WRD-KEY-04; spec §7 corrected.

title: Byte-reproducible extension payload
statement: A clean checkout at a release tag produces a byte-identical extension payload in two isolated builders, with an approved SHA-256.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C6.

title: Published store payload matches approved artifact
statement: The published store payload is compared with the approved artifact, and any unexplained file/permission/CSP difference blocks release.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C6.

title: Two-person least-privilege publisher authority
statement: Publisher authority is least-privilege, phishing-resistant, recoverable, and two-person controlled; no long-lived publishing secret is committed or printed by CI.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C6. Trust Wallet lost $7-8.5M to a leaked CWS publisher key (research L9).

title: Origin/build-ID lifecycle fails closed
statement: Creation requires the stored origin to equal the permitted production origin and the stored rp_id_hash to equal SHA-256(stored origin); an assertion is accepted only when authenticatorData.rpIdHash equals the stored rp_id_hash AND the parsed clientDataJSON.origin equals the stored origin byte-for-byte. cluster_tag is caller-attested and is not the boundary; the pinned production origin is.
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan G4/C1a). rp_id_hash = SHA-256 of the exact chrome-extension://<id> origin is immutable SmartAccount state with no migration instruction; blocks public account creation. Owner decision owed: freeze vs authenticated migration. WRDF-0016: the guarantee rests on origin binding (rp_id_hash), not cluster_tag (transcript.rs:99-106 documents cluster_tag is caller-attested and does not identify the landing cluster); the cluster_tag refusal is an honest-client accidental-use guard only. WRDF-0027: origin (variable bytes) and rp_id_hash (32-byte digest) are separate stored fields (root_verify/mod.rs:211-221) — the statement now names the typed comparisons rather than comparing a string with a digest.

title: Strict-DER parsing and mandatory low-S normalization
statement: Every browser WebAuthn assertion is parsed with strict DER (trailing bytes, non-minimal lengths, r/s out of range rejected), converted to fixed 64-byte compact form, and unconditionally low-S normalized before submission; a recorded real high-S Chrome assertion passes the on-chain precompile end to end only after normalization.
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan G3/C2a). Spec:60/:232 make low-S normalization mandatory; the precompile rejects high-S and Chrome emitted high-S on the first real sample. Blocks C3/V4. C3 signing and V4's create ceremony consume ONLY assertionToCompact() output.

title: Swap quote-source independence
statement: Both the primary and the check quote are bound to one canonical QuoteIntent (approval id + exact message digest, account, cluster, input/output mint pubkeys and decimals, ExactIn/ExactOut mode, base-unit amount, slippage/fee convention); the divergence-checked adverse quantity is net output after fees for ExactIn and total required input after fees for ExactOut, computed with checked integer math; >300 bps divergence blocks unoverridably, a stale primary re-quote that changes the intent invalidates the approval, and a check quote sharing the primary's upstream renders as no independent check, never as agreement.
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan G5/C4b). The quote-sanity check is the only price defence and is entirely off-chain (research L9 oracle/MEV lane). WRDF-0019: a dimensionless 3% is meaningless until both quotes describe the same economic quantity; C4b now defines QuoteIntent, the divergence denominator/rounding, and 300 bps. WRDF-0019 round-2: output-only divergence renders agreement for an adverse ExactOut input quote; the compared quantity is mode-dependent (input for ExactOut).

title: Vanity varies only a public salt, never a signing secret
statement: Vanity search varies only a 32-byte salt; it never generates or exports a signing secret, and the trusted client independently re-derives a worker result.
notes: Seeded by V0 (campaign plan). Warden derives the PDA from Keccak256("WARDEN/seed/v1"||root_pubkey33||salt32); the feature searches salts locally and preserves the passkey root. Implemented by vanity V1-V3. WRDF-0025: the salt is salt32 = job_nonce24 || counter64_le — a 192-bit CSPRNG job nonce plus a disjoint u64 counter (parallel-worker lanes), not a full 32-byte random value; CSPRNG failure / nonce reuse / counter wrap reject.

title: 1-4 ASCII Base58 chars enforced at every layer
statement: Every layer enforces 1-4 ASCII Base58 characters and exact prefix/suffix plus capitalization semantics; stale or mutated jobs cannot become the selected account.
notes: Seeded by V0. Base58 excludes only 0/O/I/l; do not copy /opt/vanity-bot's fixed-44-char first-symbol or J rule. Suffix + case-insensitive default; exact capitalization optional with a slower-search warning.

title: Create ceremony binds selected salt to root/config
statement: The create ceremony and post-confirmation readback bind the selected salt/address to root, program id, cluster/config, bump, and initial policy before funding or receive UI is enabled.
notes: Seeded by V0. Freeze program id/cluster/seed-domain before any long search. V4 integration waits for client C1a (origin) + C2a (strict-DER/low-S the ceremony consumes) + C3 (immutable approval record) + C4 (exact-byte decode the readback checks) — WRDF-0020.

title: Local, auditable, telemetry-free v1 generation
statement: v1 generation is local, bundled, source-auditable, and emits no wallet-linkable telemetry or private-key-shaped output.
notes: Seeded by V0. The worker returns only salt/owner-seed/address/bump metadata; a static+runtime test rejects fields matching privateKey/secretKey/mnemonic/recovery/assertion/credential.

title: Structured events on every value/policy transition
statement: execute/swap/transfer emit a structured event on every successful bucket debit and every cap rejection, and freeze/unfreeze emit freeze events; the notifier counts BucketDebited and freeze-transition events only from a finalized transaction with meta.err == null (a rolled-back debit's surviving log is not a spend), and treats CapRejected/DeniedInstructionRejected as failed-transaction signals. Each event has a replay-safe identity (transaction signature + outer/inner instruction index + event ordinal) so a reconnect/backfill/restart cannot double-count a legitimate repeated debit.
notes: Seeded by C0/V0 tranche (campaign plan G-5E). Task 5 completion requirement (5E): BucketDebited/CapRejected/FreezeSet events with tests on both root and session paths. Trail of Bits rated Squads logging insufficient for off-chain attack detection. WRDF-0022: a BucketDebited logged before a later same-tx failure survives under the failed tx; notifier-boundary semantics (finalized + meta.err==null) are part of the invariant. WRDF-0022 round 6: payload dedup is unsafe (two identical debits are legitimate); identity is by signature+instruction+ordinal. WRDF-0022 round 7: Task 5E must also prove the event set is COMPLETE (every debit/rejection/freeze path emits) and source-authenticated (events come from the warden program id, not a look-alike); finalized at Task 5 implementation.

title: Upgrade authority is the derived Squads vault PDA
statement: The deployment gate authenticates Warden's canonical ProgramData (via the pinned Program account + BPF loader ownership) and requires its upgrade authority to be the derived canonical vault PDA of a multisig whose COMPLETE audited configuration is pinned and attested from reviewed config: program id, multisig pubkey, member pubkey set AND per-member permission masks, threshold, time-lock, configAuthority == default, no actionable stale/pre-approved proposal state, and the audited Squads code hash; Squads' own upgrade governance is the documented trust-root terminus. The byte-level field list and fixtures are finalized at Task 11R implementation against the pinned Squads IDL.
notes: Seeded by C0+V0 round-1 (WRDF-0017, critical). Comparing authority against an operator-supplied 'expected' + a separate healthy-multisig check lets a single-key authority pass with an unrelated multisig. Owned by Task 11R. WRDF-0017 round 4: a non-default configAuthority can change members/threshold directly (Squads IDL), so the autonomous default (or an attested approved config authority) must be asserted. WRDF-0017 round 5: the ProgramData must be authenticated via Warden's pinned Program account + loader ownership, not taken as an unnamed account. WRDF-0017 round 6: a Squads program id is not code identity while upgradeable; pin the audited Squads code hash and terminate the trust root there (THREATMODEL external assumption). WRDF-0017 round 7 + WRDF-0028: added per-member permission masks and no-actionable-stale-proposal (a proposal Approved under an earlier weak config can still execute); the exhaustive field inventory is a Task 11R implementation artifact, closing the pre-spec regress. WRDF-0029: 'no actionable stale state' covers ConfigTransactions and batches too, not only VaultTransactions; the per-mechanism enumeration is the Task 11R artifact.

title: Adapter selectors match on-chain Registry at deploy
statement: The deployment gate authenticates the canonical Registry PDA (owner, discriminator, version) and attests its COMPLETE reviewed configuration against pinned config: every adapter selector re-derived from source (Anchor sighash from the IDL where one exists, per-program instruction tag otherwise) and diffed (missing, extra, wrong, or duplicate selectors and role-validator mismatches reject), plus the allowlist `lists` and the `treasury` fee destination. The byte-level field list and fixtures are the Task 3/deploy-time implementation artifact against the Registry layout.
notes: Seeded by C0+V0 round-1 (WRDF-0018). DEPLOY-GATE check 3, unimplemented; needs the Registry (Task 3) and selector rules (Task 5). NOT covered by Task 11R — its own deliverable; Task 11 DONE requires both this and WRD-DEP-01. WRDF-0030: the Registry carries more security state than selectors (lists determine session authorization; treasury is the mandatory swap-fee destination) — attest the complete reviewed config, byte-level list at implementation (mirrors the WRD-DEP-01 terminus).
